story.head: Jack Hughes wins it in overtime
paras: The Red Wings’ Anton Johansson picked up his first NHL point. Evan Rodrigues scored his first goal for New Jersey early in the first to open the scoring. Emmitt Finnie tied it up for Detroit late in the period. There were five goals in the second period alone. Michael Brandsegg-Nygård put the Red Wings up 2-1 early in the period. Anthony Mantha scored his first goal for New Jersey midway through the period to tie it 2-2. Nico Hischier put the Devils up 3-2 on the power play a little over three minutes later. Alex DeBrincat tied it up for Detroit just under five minutes later, and Jesper Bratt put the Devils ahead 4-3 less than two minutes later. DeBrincat scored his second of the night early in the third to tie it 4-4. Jack Hughes won it a little over a minute into overtime. Bratt and Jack Hughes each had a goal and two assists.

The Devils owned the chances, outshooting the Red Wings 37-27, and still had to sweat it out in overtime. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Devils win in regulation about seven in ten. Jake Allen made 23 saves for the Devils, and John Gibson stopped 32 of 37.

Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Red Wings hit three posts and came up a goal short. The Devils improved to 3-3-0, and the Wings dropped to 1-3-2.
